newsitem.title: ANGOLA: S.Africa's Mbeki says fresh Zaire talks still on.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mbeki says fresh Zaire talks still on.

text.p: South Africa, mediating in the Zaire conflict, said on Wednesday it still believed a second meeting would take place next week between President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila.
South African Deputy President Thabo Mbeki, on a whirlwind tour of six African countries to discuss the crisis, met Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos in Luanda on Wednesday.

"We still believe the meeting will take place next week, but before that meeting can take place we thought it necessary to consult with all those who are playing a constructive role in resolving the crisis in Zaire," Mbeki told reporters afterwards.

Mobutu and Kabila held inconclusive talks at the weekend in their first face-to-face encounter, aboard a South African naval vessel off the coast of Congo. South Africa said they agreed to meet again within 10 days.
But Mobutu on Wednesday left Zaire's capital, Kinshasa, on a two-day trip to Gabon, sparking rumours in the city that he was leaving the country for good.
Mbeki said he believed Mobutu would return to Kinshasa after attending an African mini-summit in Gabon's capital, Libreville.
He said he had spoken personally to Kabila on Tuesday night and reminded him of his promise to halt his forces from advancing on Kinshasa.
"I spoke to him last night. He told me that he had ordered his men to stop advancing on all fronts and gave me his assurance that they were not moving forward," he said.
Mediators including the United Nations, the United States and South Africa are trying to prevent further bloodshed in Zaire's civil war and arrange a peaceful transition of power.
A venue for the second Mobutu-Kabila meeting has not been named.

Mbeki was also due to visit Tanzania and Rwanda. After a stopover in Pretoria he was due to meet Kabila in Lubumbashi, Zaire, and also planned to travel to Kinshasa for talks with Mobutu on Friday before heading to Brazzaville, Congo, and Gabon.
Dos Santos did not speak to journalists. His government has been accused by Mobutu of backing the rebels.
